cues.text: Let's work through the address one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight dot ten dot seventy-seven, slash twenty-six.
A slash twenty-six has sixty-four addresses per block.
The blocks begin at zero, sixty-four, one hundred and twenty-eight, and one hundred and ninety-two.
Seventy-seven falls in the second block.
So its network ends in sixty-four, broadcast ends in one hundred and twenty-seven, and usable addresses run from sixty-five to one hundred and twenty-six.
Four slash twenty-sixes fit in one slash twenty-four.
If you need fifty hosts, find the smallest H for which two to the power H, minus two, is at least fifty.
Six host bits give sixty-two usable addresses, leaving twenty-six network bits.
If you need at least six equal subnets from a slash twenty-four, borrow three bits.
That gives eight slash twenty-seven subnets, each with thirty usable addresses.
Variable Length Subnet Masking, or VLSM, allocates different block sizes and starts with the largest requirement.
Our example uses one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight dot fifty dot zero slash twenty-four.
Segment A needs a hundred hosts, so allocate dot zero slash twenty-five.
Usable one through one hundred and twenty-six, broadcast one hundred and twenty-seven.
Segment B needs fifty, so start at dot one twenty-eight slash twenty-six.
Usable one twenty-nine through one ninety, broadcast one ninety-one.
C needs twenty-five, so dot one ninety-two slash twenty-seven: usable one ninety-three through two twenty-two, broadcast two twenty-three.
D needs ten, so dot two twenty-four slash twenty-eight: usable two twenty-five through two thirty-eight, broadcast two thirty-nine.
Dot two forty slash twenty-eight remains.
No overlap.
Reserve gateway and infrastructure addresses.

CIDR can aggregate aligned consecutive prefixes: one ninety-two dot one sixty-eight dot zero dot zero slash twenty-four through the corresponding third octet three network fit one slash twenty-two starting at zero.
Longest prefix match chooses the most specific matching route.
Ordinary IPv6 LANs often use slash sixty-four for stateless autoconfiguration; don't subtract broadcast and network addresses as in IPv4.
